verdict.rationale: Vast.ai documents Volumes as persistent storage that survives instance destruction and can be reattached to new instances, so the core of the story (data outliving a rental) is delivered. However, the docs describe these as "local" volumes on the host, not network-attached storage portable across machines. One user's wish that persistent disks were easier to work with is not a concrete contradiction. Missing for 10: evidence of network-attached (cross-host) storage, documented reattachment across different machines, and hands-on corroboration of datasets and checkpoints persisting.

support.subject: As a developer, I can attach persistent network storage that survives instance teardown, so datasets and checkpoints outlive any single GPU rental

citations.quote: Volumes provide persistent storage that survives instance destruction and can be reattached to new instances.
Volumes - Persistent local storage that survives instance deletion
You will see an option labeled Local volume with a + (plus) button next to it.
The Storage page allows you to easily access and manage your volumes - storage that can be attached to your instances for data storage.
